rationale: Symmetric 4h funding-directional logic was tested because extreme perpetual funding can reflect crowded positioning, accumulated carry cost, liquidation vulnerability, and arbitrage pressure toward mean reversion. The strategy fades positive funding with short exposure, fades negative funding with long exposure, and stays flat near zero funding to avoid unsupported cost. RETROSPECTIVE: this plan was authored after execution as part of WP-6c to extend the schema grammar to the remaining concluded candidates. The original H-001 pre-registration lives in research/hypotheses/H-001/HYPOTHESIS.md and was not schema-validated at the time.
hypothesis_to_test: A symmetric funding-directional strategy on BTCUSDT perpetual 4h bars will generate OOS Sharpe >= 1.0 net of fees, capture both crowded-long and crowded-short regimes, outperform passive long BTC on a risk-adjusted basis, and survive walk-forward validation with efficiency > 0.5.

additional_criteria: OOS Sharpe >= 1.0 net of modeled costs
Gate 2 passes under current evaluator semantics: dsr_val > 0.95 versus the expected maximum-SR benchmark from the registered trial count
Max drawdown <= 20% in any walk-forward fold
Parameter sensitivity: +/-25% parameter shift keeps Sharpe within 70% of baseline
No single 90-day window contributes > 60% of total PnL
Kill criteria from H-001 HYPOTHESIS.md apply: OOS Sharpe < 0.3, max drawdown > 35%, both long and short legs unprofitable, or funding-rate predictability no better than random

data_requirements: No separate IS/OOS split convention existed in repo truth for this baseline; DEC-0001 records full-period Sharpe in both trial-log Sharpe fields
